title: Tighten up, buck and hook him
summary: Tighten up means work at the same speed; buck is an inmate's strike over food; hook him means get to work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I notice on this record Work songs That Sheer and Welch Will be talking I believe it's Sheer and Welch I forgot Maybe the anemoses In that too But You talk about Tighten up

Well, I'm more sure That was me That spoke that word Of tighten up Well, tighten up Means that You be working Probably six of us Working Well, about three of them Is dragging around And if work ain't going Out fast enough Well, you probably see The balls coming Well, tighten up That means Let's everybody Get the same speed And get just alike So there won't be no heat Put on nobody And the heat Mean is Is this What they really call Is the heat Well, that's the demand Is on your time He watching you And see that you're not working Whenever he catch you not working Well, then You know your job Is to work And when you're not working Well, then you can look For what's never fall Let it fall on you Not on everybody If I'm not working Well, then he's supposed To tell me about it Don't come throw the weight On everybody And that tightens up That really means That for everybody Let's work together That was the word That I give them Let's tighten up And another word That we use in there Says let's buck But some people May not know What the word A buck mean Well, the word A buck would mean Say we'd have Something for none Or we didn't want it Well, we wouldn't eat it Well, we buck On to something Nobody eat it That's just the same As a union Would be striking On a nickel more On his eye of a salary It's just the same Thing it is With the man here So the union Bucks on his work In the streets For a nickel more On his salary The inmate A buck on his Because he only gets What he eats and where If he don't get that He have a legal right To buck For what he want Well, buck That's what bucks means But in the streets Union don't sell Less bucks They're less strike So An inmate don't have No strike He has a buck
Well now when you're Out there working Cutting can They say hook him What does that mean?
